title: Inbound lead, quote and proposal follow-up

gates.text: Truth and grounding: every price, date, lead time, guarantee, review, customer example and availability claim is in the confirmed facts or the lead's own message. Gaps use [NEEDS FACT: ...]. No invented discounts, slots or 'spaces left'.

Consent and compliance: calls only where the lead gave a number for that purpose or asked to be called; SMS only with text consent or after the lead texted first, identifying the business and honouring STOP; no marketing emails without marketing consent; any opt-out ends contact on every channel; contact only at reasonable hours.

Format: each message has one job and one ask; emails 150 words or fewer; texts one or two short sentences; voicemails under 20 seconds; no message that is only 'just checking in' or 'any update?'; quote follow-up at most 4 touches unless the lead re-engages; plan marked for owner approval.
Ethics: no false urgency or scarcity, no guilt or shaming, no criticism of competitors or the lead's other quotes, no arguing after a no, no more than 2 unanswered call attempts.

anchors.1: Generic acknowledgement ('Thanks for your enquiry, we'll be in touch') that answers nothing.
anchors.3: Answers the question but ignores the lead's details, or the next step is vague ('let me know').
anchors.5: Answers the actual question in the first two lines, echoes a specific detail the lead gave, asks at most two deciding questions, and offers one concrete next step with options.

anchors.1: Template copy that could go to any lead.
anchors.3: Uses the lead's name and job type but not their specifics or words.
anchors.5: Reflects the lead's own words, job details and constraints throughout; nothing generic.

anchors.1: Repeats 'just checking in' or the same pitch; no plan or endless chasing.
anchors.3: Sensible timing but touches add little new.
anchors.5: Cadence matches the situation (day 0/2/5-7/10-14 for quotes); every touch adds new information, proof or an easier path to yes; ends with a clear close-out.

anchors.1: Argues, dismisses, discounts without basis, or criticises a competitor.
anchors.3: Addresses the objection but with assertion rather than proof, or skips the next step.
anchors.5: Acknowledges in the lead's words, clarifies if needed, answers with one real proof item from the facts, and offers a smaller or reversible step; accepts a second no.

anchors.1: No ask, or 'let me know your thoughts'.
anchors.3: An ask exists but is open-ended or high-effort.
anchors.5: A specific, easy ask (two options, a date, or a one-word reply); any hold or deadline is real.

anchors.1: Call or SMS scripts are monologues, pushy, or used without consent.
anchors.3: Scripts are usable but miss permission, discovery or a written confirmation step.
anchors.5: Call script opens with reason and permission, has 2-3 discovery questions, recaps and books a next step; voicemail and SMS are short, identify the business and fit consent.

anchors.1: Pushy, needy, guilt-laden or corporate call-centre voice.
anchors.5: Warm, confident and plain, like a good owner talking to a neighbour; respectful of the lead's time and decision.

anchors.1: Loose messages with no timing, channel or stop rule.
anchors.3: Timing and channels given but stop conditions or open facts missing.
anchors.5: Situation, allowed channels with reasons, each touch's timing and text, prepared objection answers, stop conditions and [NEEDS FACT] list all present and ready for owner approval.
